author: Akihiro-Tabuchi
title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - tbb12.dll locked (Access denied) on Windows self-hosted runner
signature: remove item cannot remove item access to the path is denied unauthorizedaccessexception|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Expand-Archive step fails extracting openvino_tests.zip because tbb12.dll from the previous package extraction is still locked by another process (Access denied).

key_errors: Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step uses PowerShell Expand-Archive -Force, which first tries to delete existing files on the self-hosted Windows runner (ov-dmz-35) before overwriting them. tbb12.dll from a prior job's extracted install directory was still held open by another process (likely a lingering test/runner process or antivirus scan on this persistent self-hosted machine), so Remove-Item failed with UnauthorizedAccessException and the whole Expand-Archive command aborted with exit code 1. This is unrelated to the PR's content (a GPU build/CMake change) and is a known class of transient file-lock failure on persistent self-hosted Windows runners that do not get a clean workspace between jobs.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible on demand; requires a stale handle on tbb12.dll in C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin on runner 'ov-dmz-35' left over from a previous job. Locally: run the GPU unit test job's 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step twice in a row without cleaning the install dir while a process (e.g. a previous ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe or antivirus) still has tbb12.dll open, and PowerShell's Expand-Archive -Force will fail removing it the same way.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'GPU unit tests' job on the merge-queue run; the lock is typically transient and a retry recreates/overwrites cleanly once the holding process exits.

Add a pre-step on self-hosted Windows GPU runners to ensure the workspace install directory is fully removed (with retries) before extraction, instead of relying on Expand-Archive -Force to replace locked files in place.
Investigate whether a prior job step (gtest process or antivirus) is not releasing handles on tbb12.dll on runner ov-dmz-35 promptly after the previous job completes.
Consider using a fresh/ephemeral workspace per job on this self-hosted pool, or an explicit taskkill of leftover test processes before extraction.
prevention_strategies: Ensure self-hosted Windows runners used for GPU unit tests clean their workspace (or forcibly release file handles) between consecutive jobs before extracting new packages; prefer deleting and recreating the install directory over in-place overwrite with Expand-Archive -Force.
historical_context: No prior pattern record exists for this exact tbb12.dll/Extract-step lock signature. A related but distinct Windows file-lock pattern (JS API E2E Electron cleanup failing with 'Permission denied' removing electron.exe/dll, signature_hash 85df26485ff568d8, seen 17 times) shows this class of self-hosted Windows runner file-lock flakiness recurs across different jobs/files; this is the first occurrence specifically for the GPU unit tests package extraction step.
